This chapter gives a ﬁrst introduction to the theory of Coxeter groups.
Chapter 2 Reﬂection Groups and Coxeter Groups
This chapter explains why reﬂection groups are Coxeter groups, motivating the general deﬁnition of
Coxeter groups.
Chapter 3 The Hecke Algebra and Kazhdan-Lusztig Polynomials
The Hecke algebra associated to a Coxeter system (W, S) is a Z[v, v−1]-algebra that recovers the group
algebra Z [W] under the specialization v 7→1. It has two important bases, namely, the standard basis
and a certain self-dual basis called the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, with the change of basis between the tw

blocks.title: Page 3
blocks.content:
diagrammatic descriptions of two diﬀerent bases for these bimodules.
Part III Historical Context: Category O and the Kazhdan-Lusztig Conjectures
This part places Soergel bimodules in context, describing the connections between them and the other
incarnations of the Hecke category.
Chapter 13 Category O and the Kazhdan-Lusztig Conjectures
This chapter gives a historical introduction to the Kazhdan-Lusztig conjectures [D. Kazhdan and G.
Lusztig, Invent. Math. 53, 165–184 (1979; Zbl 0499.20035)], beginning with Verma’s thesis [D. N. Verma,
Bull. Am. Math. Soc. 74, 160–166 (1968; Zbl 0157.07604)]

Part V Special Topics
This part oﬀers a sampling of more advanced topics, ranging over cell theory and Hecke algebra repre-
sentaions (Chapter 22) and their connections to knot theory (Chapter 21), categorical diagonalization
(Chapter 23), diagrammatics for individual Soergel bimodules (Chapter 24), Koszul duality for category
O, reinterpreted using Soergel bimodules (Chapters 25 and 26), and the situation in positive characteristic
(Chapter 27).
Chapter 21 Connections to Link Invariants
This chapter relates the quantum group of gln and the Hecke algebra of the symmetric group Sm through
a qua

of the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis. This chapter deﬁnes the p-canonical basis, describing how it is computed
in practice by use of the local intersection form. The chapter presents examples that demonstrate how
it diﬀers from the Kazhdan-Lusztig basis, and the advantages of the diagrammatic Hecke category over
Soergel bimodules in positive characteristic. The chapter ﬁnally indicates the relation of the p-canonical
basis to parity complexes on the ﬂag variety and its relevance to modular representation theory.
